expectations.text: Identifies 'real-time' and 'automatically' as over-engineering signals requiring Dummy-to-Dynamic or Put-on-Crutches
expectations.evidence: The output mentions that "'Automatically' and 'real-time' add cross-cutting quality constraints that are often better validated incrementally rather than all at once" and notes them as signals. However, it never names the specific techniques 'Dummy-to-Dynamic' or 'Put-on-Crutches', which the assertion requires.

expectations.text: Identifies that 3 channels (email, SMS, in-app) behind 'and' are separate stories
expectations.evidence: The output explicitly states: "The word 'and' appears between three delivery channels, which is the clearest signal that the story contains parallel tracks that can be delivered independently." Stories 2, 4, and 5 each cover a single channel independently.

expectations.text: Defers 'based on notification preferences' as a later story — the first story uses hardcoded or default behavior
expectations.evidence: The output makes the notification preference model Story 1 (the very first story), rather than deferring it. All subsequent stories depend on Story 1's preferences. The first notification-sending story (Story 2) already filters by preferences from Story 1. No story uses hardcoded or default behavior as a crutch.

expectations.text: Applies Put-on-Crutches (#9): proposes a manual or simplified notification mechanism before building the real automated real-time system
expectations.evidence: Story 2 deliberately uses polling instead of real-time push ('no real-time push yet (polling is acceptable)'), and Story 3 is the upgrade to real-time. This is the Put-on-Crutches pattern in practice — a simplified mechanism first — even though the pattern is not named explicitly.

expectations.text: The first story delivers value via a single channel (e.g. email only), not all three simultaneously
expectations.evidence: Story 2 is the first story that actually delivers notifications to users, and it delivers via in-app only. Stories 4 and 5 add email and SMS independently afterward. No story delivers all three channels simultaneously.

expectations.text: Proposes at least 5 distinct stories covering the progression from manual/simple to automated/real-time
expectations.evidence: The output proposes exactly 5 distinct stories: (1) notification preference model, (2) in-app notifications with polling, (3) real-time in-app via WebSocket/SSE, (4) email notifications, (5) SMS notifications. These cover a clear progression from simple baseline to automated real-time delivery.
